question.text: Manager A has IC = 0.10 and breadth = 100. Manager B has IC = 0.20 and breadth = 25. Which manager has the higher Information Ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: IR_A = 0.10 × √100 = 0.10 × 10 = 1.00. IR_B = 0.20 × √25 = 0.20 × 5 = 1.00. Both deliver the same IR via different skill/breadth mixes. The Trap: The non-linearity of breadth (√) vs linearity of IC means higher-skill/lower-breadth and lower-skill/higher-breadth can arrive at identical productivity. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B-specific. Overlaps slightly with XV's active-manager evaluation concepts. Manager's Pro-Tip: When picking sub-advisors, you want high IC even at lower breadth — transaction costs eat the breadth advantage, which the formula ignores.
